				<td valign="top" style="width:71.10pt;padding:0pt;">
					<p style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
						<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Item 1</font></p>
				</td>
				<td valign="top" style="width:432.00pt;padding:0pt;">
					<p style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
						<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">BUSINESS</font></p>
				</td>
			</tr>
		</table></div>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The A.T. Cross Company (the &#x201C;Company&#x201D;) has tw</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">o reportable segments: Cross Accessory Division (&#x201C;CAD&#x201D;) and Cross Optical Group (&#x201C;COG&#x201D;).&nbsp;&nbsp;For certain financial information with respect to these segments, see Note K to the Company's consolidated financial statements included in Item 8 of this Annual Report on Form 10-K.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Cross Accessory Division</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">We manufacture and market fine quality writing instruments under the Cross</font><sup style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&#xAE;</sup><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> brand consisting of ballpoint pens, fountain pens, Selectip</font><sup style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&#xAE;</sup><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> rolling ball pens and mechanical pencils.&nbsp;&nbsp;We also manufacture and market a variety of refills for most of our product types.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition to Cross-branded writing instruments, CAD manufactures and markets a FranklinCovey line of entry level price point refillable writing instruments.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company is an original equipment manufacturer (&#x201C;OEM&#x201D;) of writing instruments.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition to writing instruments, we also design and market a variety of personal and business accessories including leather goods, reading glasses, desk sets and stationery.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company has license agreements with a third party to develop and sell Cross</font><sup style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&#xAE;</sup><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> watches and cufflinks.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company launches new pen products and other personal accessories on a bi-annual basis.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Our writing instruments are offered in a variety of styles and materials at various price points.&nbsp;&nbsp;They are packaged and sold as individual units or in matching sets.&nbsp;&nbsp;The majority of writing instrument sales occur at suggested retail price points between approximately $22 and $50.&nbsp;&nbsp;We believe we are a market leader in the United States at these price points.&nbsp;&nbsp;Products in this price range include: Classic Century</font><sup style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&#xAE;</sup><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, Calais, Aventura</font><sup style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&#xAE;</sup><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, Stratford, Cross Contour, Cross Edge, Cross Click, Bailey, Beverly, and selected ATX</font><sup style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&#xAE;</sup><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> writing instruments.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Cross Townsend</font><sup style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&#xAE;</sup><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, Sauvage, Cross Sentiment, C-Series, Apogee</font><sup style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&#xAE;</sup><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, Cross Affinity, Masquerade, Century II, Tech3 and Tech4 lines as well as selected Classic Century and ATX writing instruments provide the Company a presence in the $55 to $300 price range.&nbsp;&nbsp;Certain Classic Century, Cross Townsend and Special Edition writing instruments are priced over $300.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Sable, Nile, Revere, Sage and Parasol writing instrument product lines are sold to the Company's self-serve channels of distribution including the office superstore customers.&nbsp;&nbsp;The FranklinCovey brand provides the Company a presence in the under $10 suggested retail price range for a ballpoint pen.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Cross</font><sup style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&#xAE;</sup><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> leather goods range in price from $40 to $145, reading glasses are priced at $30, watch prices range between $100 and $330, desk sets are priced at $225, cufflinks from $50 to $80 and stationery from $20 to $25.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Company emphasizes styling, innovation, craftsmanship and quality in the design and production of all of its products.&nbsp;&nbsp;All Cross-branded writing instruments carry a full warranty of unlimited duration against mechanical failure.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our watches are sold with a limited two-year warranty, and leather goods are sold with a limited one-year warranty.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Globally, Cross Accessory Division products are sold at over 10,000 points of distribution in over 80 countries by our direct sales force and manufacturers' agents or representatives.&nbsp;&nbsp;They are sold in the United States in over 5,500 retailers, directly to consumers via the Company's website, www.cross.com, and at the Cross</font><sup style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&#xAE;</sup><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> retail store.&nbsp;&nbsp;Sales outside the United States are made to foreign distributors and retailers worldwide by the Company and its wholly-owned subsidiaries.&nbsp;&nbsp;Retail accounts include: gift stores, department stores, jewelers, stationery, office supply and pen specialty stores, and United States military post exchanges.&nbsp;&nbsp;Wholesale accounts distribute products to retail outlets in those countries where the Company does not maintain a direct sales force or to those that purchase in small quantities.&nbsp;&nbsp;Advertising specialty representatives market products to business accounts that</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> are</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> typically engraved or display a name or emblem and are used for gifts, sales promotions, incentives or advertising.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Cross Optical Group</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Company's COG segment consists of its wholly-owned subsidiary, Cross Optical Group, Inc., which was formed on January 2, 2010</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">is the legal entity of our two sunglass brands: Costa</font><sup style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&#xAE;</sup><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> and Native</font><sup style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&#xAE;</sup><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;Costa was acquired in 2003 and Native was purchased in 2008.&nbsp;&nbsp;This business designs, manufactures and markets premium, high-quality, </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">high-performance </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">polarized sunglasses under the</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">se</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> brand names.&nbsp;&nbsp;Combined, our brands offer </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">sunglasses in </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">more than </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">88</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> styles and 25 lens options</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">,</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">most </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">at suggested retail price points between approximately $</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">8</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">9 and $2</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">79</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Costa expanded its offerings in 2011 to include prescription sunglasses at suggested retail price points between approximately $300 and $750.&nbsp;&nbsp;The COG segment also sells apparel and accessory products such as hats, t-shirts, cords, cases and backpacks. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Our sunglass</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> products </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">are sold by employee representatives and manufacturers' agents to </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">approximately </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">7</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">,600 retail</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> accounts throughout the United States.&nbsp;&nbsp;Retail accounts include optical and sunglass specialty shops, department stores and sporting goods retailers.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Costa and Native sunglasses are sold with a lifetime warranty against </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">manufacturer&#x2019;s </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">defects in materials and workmanship.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">

		<p style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt"><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Raw Materials</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Company's CAD segment obtains raw materials for use in writing instruments from both domestic and foreign suppliers.&nbsp;&nbsp;Metal</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> and</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> plastic pen parts are obtained from the United States (&#x201C;U.S.&#x201D;), China, Germany, Japan, India, Malaysia, and Switzerland.&nbsp;&nbsp;Coated parts are procured from the U.S. and China.&nbsp;&nbsp;Ink is procured from the U.S., Germany, China and Japan.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The majority of component materials for the COG segment are imported from highly specialized manufacturers located in Europe and Asia.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">To maintain the highest level of product quality, </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">the Company relies</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> on a limited number of domestic and foreign suppliers for certain raw materials and manufacturing technologies.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company may be adversely affected in the event that these suppliers cease operations or if pricing terms become less favorable.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company believes, but cannot be assured</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">,</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> that the raw materials currently supplied by these vendors could be obtained from other sources and that the manufacturing technologies could either be developed internally or that suitably similar technologies could be located.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Patents, Licenses and Trademarks</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Company, directly or through its subsidiaries, has certain writing instrument, timepiece, accessory and optical trademark registrations and/or pending trademark applications in the United States and many foreign countries, including but not limited to its principal trademark &#x201C;CROSS,&#x201D; and the </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&#x201C;FRUSTO-CONICAL DESIGN&#x201D; on the </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">top of its writing instruments, and the trademarks </font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;">&#x201C;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">COSTA DEL MAR&#x201D; and &#x201C;NATIVE.&#x201D;&nbsp;&nbsp;The principal trademark &#x201C;CROSS&#x201D; is of fundamental importance to the CAD segment and the trademarks &#x201C;COSTA DEL MAR&#x201D;, &#x201C;COSTA&#x201D; and &#x201C;NATIVE&#x201D; are of fundamental importance to the COG segment.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company, directly or through its subsidiaries, holds certain United States and foreign writing instrument patents and/or has filed United States and foreign patent applications covering products including, but not limited to, Cross Townsend, </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Edge, Tech4</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">and</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> the Company's ball-point pen mechanism.&nbsp;&nbsp;While </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">the Company</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> pursue</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">s</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> a practice of seeking patent protection for novel inventions or designs, </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">the</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> business is not dependent upon obtaining and maintaining patents.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Seasonal Business</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The CAD segment has historically generated its highest sales in the second half of the year, approximately one-third in the fourth quarter.&nbsp;&nbsp;The COG segment has historically generated its highest sales in the first half of the year, approximately one-third in the second quarter.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Working Capital Requirements</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Writing instrument and sunglass inventory balances tend to be highest in anticipation of new product launches and before peak selling seasons.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company offers, and may offer in the future, extended payment terms, primarily to domestic retail writing instrument customers, at certain points during the year.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Customers</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Company is not dependent upon any single customer for more </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">than 5% of its</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> consolidated revenues.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Backlog of Orders</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The backlog of orders is not a significant factor in the Company's business.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

</div><hr size="3" style="color:#999999" width="100%" align="center"></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt"><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;"></font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Competition</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The global non-disposable writing instrument market is e</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">stimated to be approximately $2 </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">billion at retail.&nbsp;&nbsp;It is competitive, in particular with respect to product quality, brand recognition and price.&nbsp;&nbsp;There are</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> numerous manufacturers of ball</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">point, rolling ball and fountain pens, and mechanical pencils in the U.S. and abroad.&nbsp;&nbsp;Many of these manufacturers produce lower-priced writing instruments than those produced by the Company.&nbsp;&nbsp;Although the Comp</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">any is a major producer of ball</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">point, rolling ball and fountain pens, and mechanical pencils in the $2</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">2</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> to $50 price range, other writing instrument companies have significantly higher sales volumes from a broader product line across a wider range of prices or have greater resources as divisions of larger corporations.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company emphasizes styling, innovation, craftsmanship and quality in the design and production of all of its products.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The plano sunglass market in the U.S. is estimated to be $3.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">5</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> billion at retail.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company's COG segment under the brand names Costa and Native compete in the premium-priced ($50+ retail) sunglass market segment, which is estimated to be $2.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">4</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> billion at retail.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The prescription sunglass market segment is estimated to be approximately $5.0 billion at retail.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Many other sunglass compan</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">ies also compete in these </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">segment</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">s</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">See also the &#x201C;Risk Factors&#x201D; in Item 1A of this Annual Report on Form 10-K.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Company had expenditures for research and development of new products and improvement of existing products of approxim</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">ately $2.7 million,</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> $2.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">7</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> million and $2.8 million in 201</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">2</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, 201</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">1</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> and 20</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">10</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, respectively.&nbsp;&nbsp;For additional discussion, see &#x201C;Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations&#x201D; in Item 7 of this Annual Report on Form 10-K.</font>

				</td>
				<td valign="top" style="width:378.00pt;padding:0pt;">
					<p style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
						<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">RISK FACTORS</font></p>
				</td>
			</tr>
		</table></div>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The following section describes certain of the more prominent risks and uncertainties inherent in our operations.&nbsp;&nbsp;The risks and uncertainties below are those that we currently consider material; however, this section does not intend to discuss all possible risks and uncertainties that a company like Cross with broad international operations could experience.&nbsp;&nbsp;We are susceptible to macroeconomic downturns in the United States or abroad that may affect the general economic climate and the performance of our customers.&nbsp;&nbsp;Similarly, the price of our securities is subject to volatility due to fluctuations in general market conditions, differences in our results of operations from estimates and projections generated by the investment community, and other factors beyond our control.&nbsp;&nbsp;Further, there could be other risks and uncertainties that are not presently known to us or that may become more significant to us.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">T</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">hese Risk Factors </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">should be read </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">in conjunction with the factors discussed elsewhere in this and other of our filings with the SEC and in materials incorporated by reference in these filings.&nbsp;&nbsp;We undertake no obligation to correct or update any forward-looking statements or statements of risk related thereto for any reason.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

		</p>
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">

			<font style="display: inline;">4</font>

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">

			&nbsp;

		</p>

</div><hr size="3" style="color:#999999" width="100%" align="center"></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">We depend on the success of new products.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;Our ability to sustain profitability and growth in sales depends largely on consumer acceptance of numerous new products recently introduced and planned for introduction.&nbsp;&nbsp;Further, consumer preferences are continuously changing.&nbsp;&nbsp;The markets in which we sell are highly competitive, and there is no assurance that consumer acceptance will be realized to the degree necessary to generate continued growth in our sales and earnings.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Our global manufacturing, sales and distribution operations make us susceptible to the risks of overseas operations.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;We have sales offices and certain operations i</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">n &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">ten</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;c</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">ountries and </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">we have </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">distributors worldwide.&nbsp;&nbsp;In 201</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">2</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, approxim</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">ately </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">38</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">% o</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">f our revenue came from sales to locations outside the United States.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">We may be adversely affected in the event that global economic uncertainty erodes consumer confidence and purchasing.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Most of our products are manufactured overseas.&nbsp;&nbsp;Operating internationally exposes us to changes in export controls and other laws or regulations, as well as the general political and economic conditions, security risks,</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> natural disasters,</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> health conditions and possible disruptions in transportation networks, of the various countries in which we operate, which could result in an adverse effect on our business and results of operations in such countries.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Incorrect forecasts of consumer demand could adversely affect our results of operations.</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> The Company manufactures product based on forecasts of consumer demand.&nbsp;&nbsp;These forecasts are based on multiple assumptions.&nbsp;&nbsp;If we inaccurately forecast consumer demand we may hold inadequate, excess or obsolete inventory that would reduce our profit margins and adversely affect our results of operations and financial condition.&nbsp;&nbsp;Goodwill and other indefinite-lived intangible assets impairment analyses rely on forecasted cash flows resulting from our expectations of consumer demand.&nbsp;&nbsp;Failure to meet these forecasts could result in an impairment of goodwill or other indefinite-lived intangible assets, which would impact results of operations.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Our success depends on our ability to retain and recruit a sufficient number of qualified employees in a competitive environment.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;Our success depends</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">,</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> in part</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">,</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> on our retention and recruitment of skilled personnel, including technical, distribution, sourcing, marketing, sales, management and staff personnel.&nbsp;&nbsp;There can be no assurance that we will be able to successfully retain and recruit the key personnel that we need.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Our dependence on certain suppliers may leave us temporarily without adequate access to raw materials or products.</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp; &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">To maintain the highest level of product quality, we rely on a limited number of domestic and foreign suppliers for certain raw materials, manufacturing technologies and certain finished products.&nbsp;&nbsp;We may be adversely affected in the event that these suppliers cease operations or if pricing terms become less favorable.&nbsp;&nbsp;We believe, but cannot guarantee, that we could obtain the raw materials currently supplied by these vendors from other sources and that we could either develop the manufacturing technologies internally or locate suitably similar technologies.&nbsp;&nbsp;If we are unable to replace a key supplier we may face delays in delivering finished products according to our customers' demands, which could have an adverse effect on our financial performance.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Overseas manufacturing makes us dependent upon the performance of our overseas partners.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;As a result of our manufacturing initiative, we manufacture most of our finished products in China.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our manufacturing operations in China are supported by a local partner from whom Cross leases the building housing Cross' physical plant.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Unfavorable resolution of pending or future litigation matters could prove costly to us.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;In 2002, the Company received a so-called notice letter under </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">the </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation and Liability Act ("</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">CERCLA") from the Federal Environmental Protection Agency (&#x201C;EPA&#x201D;) alleging that the Company is a Potentially Responsible Party (&#x201C;PRP&#x201D;) in one Superfund case.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Company has reached settlement of the case and paid a settlement amount of approximately $0</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">2 million in 2010.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The EPA </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">is expected to </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">select a remedy for the Site in 201</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">3</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;At that time, the EPA will initiate an administrative process (the "Special Notice Process") pursuant to CERCLA whereby the EPA will request that those entities that the EPA contends arranged for the disposal of hazardous materials at the Site (the PRPs), undertake the selected remedy at the Site.&nbsp;&nbsp;The EPA contends that the Company is a PRP at the Site.&nbsp;&nbsp;During the Special Notice Process, the Company and the other PRPs will engage in negotiations with the EPA regarding the remedy, and among themselves regarding the contribution of each PRP to overall remediation costs.&nbsp;&nbsp;Neither the cost of the remedy nor the identity of all PRPs is known at this time.&nbsp;&nbsp;Therefore it is not possible to assess the outcome of the Special Notice Process as it may relate to the Company's contribution to remediation costs.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp; &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">If we were required to fully fund the remediation of a site, the statutory framework would allow us to pursue rights to contribution from other PRPs.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">We are involved from time to time in litigation matters.&nbsp;&nbsp;An unfavorable resolution of pending litigation could have a material adverse effect on our financial condition.&nbsp;&nbsp;Litigation may result in substantial costs and expenses and significantly divert the attention of our management regardless of the outcome.&nbsp;&nbsp;There can be no assurance that we will be able to achieve a favorable settlement of pending litigation or obtain a favorable resolution of litigation if it is not settled.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, current and future litigation, governmental proceedings or environmental matters could lead to increased costs or interruptions of our normal business operations.</font>
		</p>
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Company was named as one of approximately ninety defendants in a contribution suit brought by CCL/Unilever relating to the J.M. Mills Landfill Site (the &#x201C;Site&#x201D;), which is part of the Peterson/Puritan Superfund Site in Cumberland, Rhode Island.&nbsp;&nbsp;These complaints alleged that the Company was liable under CERCLA for contribution for Site investigation costs.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company has reached settlement of the case and paid a settlement amount of approximately $0.2 million in 2010.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The EPA </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">is expected to </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">select a remedy for the Site in 201</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">3</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">. &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">At that time, the EPA will initiate an administrative process (the "Special Notice Process") pursuant to CERCLA whereby the EPA will request that those entities that the EPA contends arranged for the disposal of hazardous materials at the Site (the PRPs), undertake the selected remedy at the Site.&nbsp;&nbsp;The EPA contends that the Company is a PRP at the Site.&nbsp;&nbsp;During the Special Notice Process, the Company and the other PRPs will engage in negotiations with the EPA regarding the remedy, and among themselves regarding the contribution of each PRP to overall remediation costs.&nbsp;&nbsp;Neither the cost of the remedy nor the identity of all PRPs is known at this time.&nbsp;&nbsp;Therefore it is not possible to assess the outcome of the Special Notice Process as it may relate to the Company's contribution to remediation costs.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Company is involved in various other litigation and legal matters that have arisen in the ordinary course of business.&nbsp;&nbsp;To its knowledge, management believes that the ultimate resolution of any of those existing matters will not have a material adverse effect on the Company's consolidated financial position or results of operations.</font>

					<p style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">

				</td>

		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Results of Operations</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Overview</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">A.T. Cross Company </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">(&#x201C;the Company&#x201D;) </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">is a designer and marketer of branded personal accessories including writing instruments, reading glasses, personal and business accessories and sunglasses.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Company operat</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">es in</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> competitive categories.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company has challenged itself to build upon its unique attributes in order to develop a vibrant, diversified and forward-looking company poised for sustainable growth and long-term profit.&nbsp;&nbsp;Such attributes include: strong brand names, an over 160 year heritage, a reputation for quality and craftsmanship, a global distribution network, and a strong balance sheet.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company established several strategic initiatives to build upon these attributes and overcome its challenges, including: becoming an innovative leader in the fine writing category, extending the Cross brand into new categories, developing avenues for diversification, streamlining its CAD operating structure and </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">seeking additional brand assets to add scale</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;COG has provided the business with an avenue of diversification and added two new brands to the Company&#x2019;s portfolio: Costa and Native.&nbsp;&nbsp;These brands uphold the Company&#x2019;s reputation as an innovative leader with award-winning high-quality products.&nbsp;&nbsp;Details on how the Company's two business segments are achieving these in</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">itiatives are presented below.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">In February 2013, t</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">he Company </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">announced that it </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">is</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">explor</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">ing</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> strategic alternatives for its Cross Accessory Division.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Company has not made a decision to pursue any specific transaction or any other strategic alternative, and there is no set timetable for the strategic review process.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Cross Accessory Division (&#x201C;CAD&#x201D;)</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Company has been a manufacturer and marketer of fine quality writing instruments since 1846.&nbsp;&nbsp;Sold primar</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">ily under the Cross brand, ball</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">point, fountain and Selectip rolling ball pens and mechanical pencils are offered in a variety of styles and finishes</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;">.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Cross also manufactures and markets a line of FranklinCovey entry level price point refillable writing instruments.&nbsp;&nbsp;Also under the Cross brand, CAD offers a variety of personal and business accessories including leather goods, reading glasses, desk sets an</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">d stationery.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Company has license agreement</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">s</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> with a third party to develop and sell Cross watches and cufflinks.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">CAD is competing vigorously to build its position in terms of product innovation, marketing and merchandising.&nbsp;&nbsp;To this end, a number of initiatives, many of which are described below, have been impleme</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">nted.&nbsp;&nbsp;In 2012, approx</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">imately 9% of</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> CAD revenue was derived from new products launche</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">d into the marketplace.&nbsp;&nbsp;In 2012</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, CAD launched </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">several </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">new writing instrument product lines:&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Cross Click, Tech4, Sauvage Forever Pearl, Special Edition Year of the Snake, a Disney Anniversary pen as well as the addition of a stylus feature to our Tech3 multifunction pen.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Company also launched </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">several gift sets for its </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">office s</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">uperstore customers for the 2012</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> holiday season. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">In 2012</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, all leather goods, reading glasses, watches, desk sets, cufflinks and statio</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">nery represented approximately 7</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">% of CAD sales.&nbsp;&nbsp;The</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> Company's stationery collection exp</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">anded in 2012 with</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> the addition of several new </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">fashionable </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">styles and colors.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">In addition to bringin</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">g new products to market in 2012</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, Cross </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">expanded the</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> global self-serve program.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company rolled out over </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">300</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> new fixtures featuring a range of reading glasses, stationery </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">and writing instruments.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Cross brand has strong consumer awareness and, more importantly, consumers associate the Cross name with innovation, quality and style.&nbsp;&nbsp;The strong awareness of our name and the positive attributes associated with our brand support the extension of the Cross brand into related personal accessory categories.&nbsp;&nbsp;CAD has moved into categories that allow us to further utilize our existing sourcing infrastructure and global distribution network.&nbsp;&nbsp;A priority for all of our brand extensions is to incorporate the quality, design and craftsmanship that consumers enjoy from Cross' fine writing instruments.&nbsp;&nbsp;We have developed a foothold in these categories and look forward to further strengthening our prese</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">nce in select categories in 2013</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Cross Optical Group (&#x201C;COG&#x201D;)</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Company's COG segment consists of its wholly-owned subsidiary</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">,</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> Cross Optical Group, Inc.&nbsp;&nbsp;This business designs, manufactures and markets high-quality, high-performance polarized sunglasses under the brand names Costa and Native.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Founded in Florida in 1983, the Costa brand has developed a superior reputation for its advanced polarized lens technology and functional frame design.&nbsp;&nbsp;Costa upholds the Company's commitment to delivering exceptional product, innovation and quality to consumers.&nbsp;&nbsp;Costa's lenses are renowned for their clarity; the patented 580 lens technology is considered by many to be </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">one of </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">the best performing sunglass lens in the marketplace.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">In 2011, Costa </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">entered into the </font>
		</p>
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">

			<font style="display: inline;">9</font>

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">

			&nbsp;

		</p>

</div><hr size="3" style="color:#999999" width="100%" align="center"></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">prescription s</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">unglass business</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;Costa&#x2019;s core market has traditionally been the saltwater fishing enthusiast in the southeastern United States.&nbsp;&nbsp;As such, </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Costa has a long-term commitment to conservation initiatives that protect and sustain</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">vital fisheries</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;Costa </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">has expanded its marketing efforts to reach consumers beyond </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">its</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> core market</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> by </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">developing consumer awareness in other fishing categories</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">geographies</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> and demographics.&nbsp;&nbsp;Costa sponsors related lifestyle ac</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">tivities such as Kenny Chesney c</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">oncert </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">t</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">our</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">s</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">sells</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> limited edition Kenny Chesney sunglasses</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;Costa's collection features a broad range of styles that appeal to a </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">wide</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> consumer demographic</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;The brand</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> is expanding geographically in both domestic and international markets.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Native, which was founded in 1994, also specializes in polarized sunglasses.&nbsp;&nbsp;Native </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">products</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> are feature-rich and are priced from $89 to $139.&nbsp;&nbsp;The collection consists primarily of high-performance sport wraps that are designed for mountain and trail enthusiasts who are active in the &#x201C;human powered sports&#x201D; such as biking, running and climbing.&nbsp;&nbsp;Native frames are very light weight and known for their exceptional fit, features sought after by professional athletes and active sport enthusiasts alike.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;Native&#x2019;s Odyssey series, launched in 2012, features the N3</font><sup style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&#x2122;</sup><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> lens; one of the most advanced polarized lenses on the market.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The creation of the Cross Optical Group has proven to be very successful.&nbsp;&nbsp;As a result, the Company is benefiting from revenue diversification and a substantial co</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">ntribution to the bottom line.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Consolidated net sales were $</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">174.6</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> million in 2011 compared to $158.3 million in 2010.&nbsp;&nbsp;The effect of foreign exchange was favorable to consolidated 2011 sales results by approximately $</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">2</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">4</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">million, or 1.5 percentage</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> points.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">CAD sales benefitted from </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">the</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> economic recovery as every region reported higher sales performance from a year ago.&nbsp;&nbsp;The effect of foreign exchange was favorable to CAD 2011 sales results by approximately $</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">2</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">4</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> million, or </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">2</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">4</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> percentage point</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">s</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">COG sales in 2011 were primarily driven by growth of the Costa brand.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The increase in Costa sales was due to new product launches aimed to appeal to</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> a non-fishing demographic</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, expanded distribution</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">,</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> an increase in revenue from </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">repairs, </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">apparel and accessories</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> as well as the 2011 introduction of Costa Rx prescription sunglasses</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;Native brand sales also increased from the prior year.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Company has no material off balance sheet arrangements.</font>

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Impact of Inflation and Changing Prices</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Company's two operating segments are subject to the effects of general inflation as well as fluctuations in foreign currencies.&nbsp;&nbsp;Policies and programs are in place to manage the potential risks in these areas.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company has generally been successful in controlling cost increases due to general inflation.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company continues to review its suppliers in order to obtain lower costs and higher quality on many of its raw materials and purchased components.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Company typically enters into foreign currency exchange contracts to economically hedge that portion of its net financial position exposed to foreign currency fluctuations.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">New Accounting Pronouncements</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">For a description of new accounting pronouncements that affect the Company and the status of the Company's implementation thereof, see the &#x201C;New Accounting Pronouncements&#x201D; section of Note A to the Company's consolidated financial statements in Item 8 of this Annual Report on Form 10-K.&nbsp;&nbsp;None are expected to have a material impact on the Company's consolidated financial position, results of operations or cash flows.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Critical Accounting Policies and Estimates</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Management's discussion and analysis of financial condition, results of operations and cash flows are based upon our consolidated financial statements, which have been prepared in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles in the United States.&nbsp;&nbsp;The preparation of these financial statements requires us to make estimates and judgments that affect the reported amounts of assets, liabilities, revenues and expenses, as well as related disclosures of contingent liabilities.&nbsp;&nbsp;We evaluate our policies and estimates on an ongoing basis, including those related to tax contingencies, inventory adjustments, warranty reserves, retirement obligations, impairment of assets and revenue recognition.&nbsp;&nbsp;Management bases its estimates on historical experience and various other assumptions that are believed to be reasonable under the circumstances, the results of</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">which form the basis for making judgments about the carrying values of assets and liabilities that are not readily apparent from other sources.&nbsp;&nbsp;Actual results may differ from these estimates under different assumptions or conditions.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">We have identified the following policies as critical to an understanding of our results of operations and financial condition.&nbsp;&nbsp;This is not a comprehensive list of our accounting policies.&nbsp;&nbsp;In many cases, the accounting treatment of a particular transaction is specifically dictated by generally accepted accounting principles, with no need for management's judgment in its application.&nbsp;&nbsp;There are also areas in which management's judgment in selecting any available alternative would not produce a materially different result.&nbsp;&nbsp;For further discussion of our accounting policies, see Note A &#x201C;Significant Accounting Policies&#x201D; to the Company's consolidated financial statements in Item 8 of this Annual Report on Form 10-K.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

		</p>
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">

			<font style="display: inline;">13</font>

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">

			&nbsp;

		</p>

</div><hr size="3" style="color:#999999" width="100%" align="center"></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"></font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Inventory Methods and Realizable Value.</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> Our global inventories are carried at the lower of cost or market, which requires us to estimate adjustments for both obsolescence and the market value we can expect to receive for our on hand inventory.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Since </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">we are required to produce our product with sufficient lead time to satisfy global distribution and expected demand during seasonal peak periods, we are subject to the risks of consumer acceptance of the products we have produced.&nbsp;&nbsp;We assess our need for obsolescence </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">and market value </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">adjustments based on a variety of factors including historical demand, future marketing plans and alternative uses for raw material and work-in-process.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Warranty Reserves.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;CAD's Cross-branded writing instruments are sold with a full warranty of unlimited duration against mechanical failure.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Costa and Native sunglasses are sold with a lifetime warranty against defects in materials and workmanship.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">In establishing the accrual for warranty costs, management analyzes trends of several factors, measured over a period of several years that impact the Company's cost to service the warranties.&nbsp;&nbsp;The most significant factors include: the operating costs of the service department, unit sales, the number of units that are returned for warranty repair and the cost of product repairs.&nbsp;&nbsp;The estimates affecting the warranty reserve are updated annually.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Retirement Obligations.</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Two critical assumptions, the discount rate and the expected return on plan assets, are important elements of pension expense and liability measurement.&nbsp;&nbsp;We evaluate these critical assumptions annually.&nbsp;&nbsp;Other assumptions involve demographic factors such as retirement, mortality, turnover and rate of compensation increases.&nbsp;&nbsp;The discount rate enables us to state expected future cash flow as a present value on the measurement date.&nbsp;&nbsp;The guideline for setting this rate is a high-quality long-term corporate bond rate.&nbsp;&nbsp;A lower discount rate increases the present value of benefit obligations and increases pension expense.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">We decreased our discount rates to 3.73% in 2012 from 4.21% in 2011 on domestic plans and to 3.3% in 2012 from 4.7% in 2011 on foreign plans, to reflect market interest rate conditions.&nbsp;&nbsp;To determine the expected long-term rate of return on the plan</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> assets, we consider the current and expected asset allocation, as well as historical and expected returns on each plan asset class.&nbsp;&nbsp;A lower expected rate of return on pension plan assets will increase pension exp</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">ense.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our long-term expected return on plan assets was 7.8% in 2012 and 2011 for domestic plans, and 2.7% in 2012 and 3.8% in 2011 for foreign plans.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Impairment </font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">of Long-Lived Assets</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp; &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Goodwill and other indefinite-lived intangible assets are not amortized but subject to annual impairment tests; more frequently if events or circumstances occur that would indicate a potential decline in their fair value.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company performs the assessment annually during the fourth quarter and on an interim basis if potential impairment indicators arise.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company has identified two reporting units, consisting of the CAD and COG segments.&nbsp;&nbsp;In 2012 and 2011, all goodwill and indefinite-lived intangibles were held by the COG segment.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">In 2011, the Company determined the fair value of the COG reporting unit&#x2019;s goodwill using established income and market valuation approaches.&nbsp;&nbsp;The test resulted in a fair value of 139% in excess of the reporting units carrying value, including the goodwill.&nbsp;&nbsp;In 2012, under Accounting Standards Update (&#x201C;ASU&#x201D;) No 2011-08, &#x201C;Testing Goodwill for Impairment,&#x201D; the Company performed a qualitative assessment to determine if further impairment testing was necessary.&nbsp;&nbsp;This qualitative assessment is intended to determine whether it is more likely than not (having a likelihood of more than 50%) that the fair value is less than its carry amount.&nbsp;&nbsp;In making its assessment, the Company considered a number of factors, such as macro-economic conditions, industry and market considerations, cost factors, segment financial performance, entity-specific events and share price.&nbsp;&nbsp;Based upon the above factors, it is considered more likely than not (having a likelihood of more than 50%) that the fair value of the COG reporting unit is more than its carrying value.&nbsp;&nbsp;Therefore based on the qualitative assessment, goodwill was not considered impaired as of November 24, 2012.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Company determined the fair value of the COG reporting unit&#x2019;s indefinite-lived intangible assets, consisting of two trade names, &#x201C;Costa&#x201D; ($3.4 million carrying value) and &#x201C;Native&#x201D; ($3.5 million carrying value), using a forward-looking relief from royalty model.&nbsp;&nbsp;The significant assumptions used in the forward-looking relief from royalty method include: revenue growth, royalty rates and discount rate.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company performed a sensitivity analysis on the significant assumptions and has determined that a change in its assumptions, as follows, would not impact its conclusion regarding the fair value of the Costa trade name: reduce projected revenue growth rates by 10%, reduce projected royalty rate by 5.0% or increase the discount rate by 100 basis points.&nbsp;&nbsp;The </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">N</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">ative trade name is more sensitive to changes in the assumptions underlying the relief from royalty method, particularly projected revenue growth rates.&nbsp;&nbsp;In order to recover the asset in full, a five year average growth rate of 10% needs to be achieved.&nbsp;&nbsp;Each 100 basis point reduction in the assumed growth rate would result in an impairment of approximately $0.1 million.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company has determined that indefinite-lived intangibles were recoverable as of December 29, 2012.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Revenue Recognition</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;Revenue recognition requires estimates of product returns, discounts and rebates at the time revenue is recognized.&nbsp;&nbsp;These estimates are based on customer communication and historical experience.&nbsp;&nbsp;Should these estimates change, there could be a material effect on revenue recognized.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Forward-Looking Statements</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

					<p style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
						<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">QUANTITATIVE AND QUALITATIVE DISCLOSURES ABOUT MARKET RISK</font></p>
				</td>
