		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Current economic conditions and market disruptions may adversely affect the Company's business and results of operations.&nbsp;&nbsp;Financial markets throughout the world have been experiencing extreme disruption in recent months, including, among other things, volatility in security prices, diminished liquidity and credit availability, rating downgrades and declining valuations of certain investments, failure and potential failures of major financial institutions and unprecedented government support of financial institutions.&nbsp;&nbsp;These developments and the related general economic downturn may adversely impact the Company's business and financial condition in a number of ways, including impacts beyond those typically associated with other recent downturns in the U.S. and foreign economies.&nbsp;&nbsp;The current tightening of credit in financial markets and the general economic downturn may adversely affect the ability of Cross' customers, suppliers, and channel partners (e.g., distributors) to obtain financing for purchases and operations.&nbsp;&nbsp;The tightening could result in a decrease in demand for the Company's products, negatively impact Cross' ability to collect its accounts receivable on a timely basis, result in additional reserves for uncollectible accounts receivable being required, and in the event of a contraction in Cross' sales, could require additional reserves for inventory obsolescence.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Foreign currency exchange rates and fluctuations in those rates may affect the Company's ability to realize projected growth rates in its sales and earnings.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company derives approxima</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">tely </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">38</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">% of its r</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">evenues from outside the United States.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company's ability to realize projected growth rates in sales and earnings could be adversely affected if the U.S. dollar strengthens significantly against foreign currencies.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Company's foreign exchange exposure is generated primarily from its international operating subsidiaries.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company seeks to minimize the impact of foreign currency fluctuations by hedging certain foreign currency denominated balance sheet positions with foreign currency forward exchange contracts.&nbsp;&nbsp;Most of these contracts are short-term, generally expire in one to three months and a 5% change in exchange rates would not subject the Company to material market risk.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;Although the Company has programs in place to manage foreign currency exchange risk on certain foreign currency denominated balance sheet positions, and on a portion of certain foreign currency denominated cash flows, significant volatility and fluctuations in the rates of exchange for the U.S. dollar against currencies</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">such as the Euro, the British Pound</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">,</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> the Chinese Renminbi</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> and the Japanese Yen could adversely affect the Company's financial position and results of operations.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Company maintains a $40 million secured line of credit with a bank.&nbsp;&nbsp;Under this agreement, the Company has the option to borrow at various interest rates depending upon the type of borrowings made and the Company's consolidated leverage ratio.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company believes that changes in interest rates would not be material to its operations, due to its anticipated level of borrowings.&nbsp;&nbsp;There w</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">as $</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">15.0</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> mi</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">llion and $</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">21</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">2</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> million outstanding under the Company's line of credit at </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">December 29, 2012</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">December 31, 2011</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, respectively.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Company entered into interest rate swap agreements that effectively fix the interest rate on a portion of its line of credit at </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">1</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">2</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">% per annum.&nbsp;&nbsp;At </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">December 29, 2012</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, the notional value of the interest rate swap was $15.0 million.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;">Basis of Presentation and Nature of Operations:</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;The consolidated financial statements include the accounts</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> of A.T. Cross Company and its subsidiaries (the &#x201C;Company&#x201D;). </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Upon consolidation, intercompany accounts and transactions are eliminated.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Company has two reportable segments: Cross Accessory Division (&#x201C;CAD&#x201D;), and Cross Optical Group (&#x201C;COG&#x201D;). </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Company's CAD segment designs, manufactures and markets writing instruments throughout the world and is an OEM of writing instruments. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Writing instrument products are sold under the Cross brand as well as the </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">FranklinCovey </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">brand. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">They include ball-point pens, fountain pens, </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">S</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">electip rolling ball pens, mechanical pencils and writing instrument accessories such as refills and desk sets. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Also under the Cross brand, CAD offers a variety of personal and business accessories including leather goods, reading glasses, desk sets an</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">d stationery.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Company has license agreement</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">s</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> with a third party to develop and sell Cross watches and cufflinks.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> The Company's COG segment designs, manufactures and markets sunglasses throughout the United States under the Costa and Native brand names. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Company evaluates segment performance based upon operating profit or loss. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Company's reportable segments are strategic business units that offer different product lines. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">They are managed separately, as each unit requires different technologies and marketing strategies.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Company operates on </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">a 52/53 week fiscal year, ending on the last Saturday closest to December 31.&nbsp;&nbsp;A fiscal year usually consists of four 13 week fiscal quarters.&nbsp;&nbsp;Fiscal 2008 was a 53 week year with 14 weeks in the fourth quarter.&nbsp;&nbsp;Fis</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">cal</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">years 2012, </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">2011</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, 2010 and 2009 were </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">52-week</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> years </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">end</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">ed December 29, 2012</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">,</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> December 31, 2011,</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">January 1, 2011 and January 2, 2010, respectively</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">. &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Company has historically recorded its highest sales in the fourth quarter.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Company considers events or transactions that occur after the balance sheet date but before the financial statements are issued to provide additional evidence relative to certain estimates or to identify matters that require additional disclosure. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Subsequent events have been evaluated to the date of issuance of these financial statements.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The accounting policies of the Company are described in this summary of significant accounting policies.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;">Accounting for Estimates:</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;The preparation of financial statements, in accordance with accounting principles</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> generally accepted in the United States of America (&#x201C;GAAP&#x201D;), requires the Company to make assumptions that affect the estimates reported in these consolidated financial statements. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Actual results may differ from these estimates. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The significant estimates in the Company's consolidated financial statements include sales returns and allowances, allowance for doubtful accounts receivable, realizable value of inventory, impairment of long-lived assets and goodwill, warranty, retirement obligations and </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">income taxes.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;">Cash Equivalents and Short-Term Investments:</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;The Company considers all highly liquid investments with a maturity of three months or less when purchased to be cash equivalents.&nbsp;&nbsp;Short-term investments are stated at fair value.&nbsp;&nbsp;Gains or losses on short-term investments, both realized and unrealized, are included in other (expense) income.&nbsp;&nbsp;At </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">December 29, 2012</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">December 31, 2011</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, approximately </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">31</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">% an</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">d &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">40</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">%, respectively, of the Company's cash and cash equivalents were on deposit with one financial institution.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;">Long-Lived Assets:</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Company reviews long-lived assets for impairment whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate that the carrying amount of an asset may not be recoverable. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Recoverability of assets to be held and used is measured by a comparison of the carrying amount of an asset to the undiscounted cash flows expected to be generated by the asset. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">If such assets are considered to be impaired, the impairment recognized is measured by the amount by which the carrying amount of the assets exceeds the fair value of the assets. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Assets to be disposed of are reported at the lower of the carrying amount or fair value, less the cost to sell.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;">Goodwill and Other Intangible Assets:</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Goodwill and certain intangible assets with indefinite lives are not amortized but are subject to annual impairment tests, more frequently if events or circumstances occur that would indicate a potential decline in their fair value. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Company has identified </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">two</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> reporting units, consisting of the CAD and COG segments. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Company performs the assessment annually during the fourth quarter and on an interim basis if potential impairment indicators arise. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Company determines the fair value of the reporting units using </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">accepted accounting standard methodologies</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> and the values of certain intangible assets with indefinite lives, consisting of two COG segment trade names, using a forward-looking relief from royalty model.</font>
		</p>

					<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0.05pt;text-align:center; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;">Revenue Recognition:</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Revenue from sales is recognized when the following criteria are met: persuasive evidence of an arrangement exists, title to the goods has passed to the customer, the sales price is fixed or determinable, and collection of the sales price is reasonably assured. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Provisions are made at the time the related revenue is recognized for estimated product returns, discounts and rebates.</font>
		</p>
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">

			<font style="display: inline;">23</font>

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">

			&nbsp;

		</p>

</div><hr size="3" style="color:#999999" width="100%" align="center"></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"></font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;">Marketing Support Costs:</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The costs of marketing support, including advertising, are charged to expense as incurred and amounted to approximatel</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">y $13.8 million, $13.7 million and</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;$</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">12.3</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> million for fiscal 201</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">2</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, 201</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">1</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> and 20</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">10</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, respectively. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Accrued marketing support expenses </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">were approximately $</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">2.5 million</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> at </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">December 29, 2012</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> and $</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">2.3</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> million at </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">December 31, 2011</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> and are included in accrued expenses and other liabilities.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;">Derivatives:</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Company has a program in place to manage foreign currency risk. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">As part of that program, the Company can enter into foreign currency exchange contracts to hedge anticipated foreign currency transactions or commitments, primarily purchases of materials and products from foreign suppliers, and certain foreign currency denominated balance sheet positions. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The terms of the contracts are generally less than </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">three</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> months. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> Forward exchange contracts generally do not qualify for hedge accounting and g</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">ains and losses are included in SG&amp;A expenses.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Company also uses interest rate swaps to manage its exposure to changing interest rates that result from variable rate debt. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">These swaps effectively fix the interest rate on a portion of the Company's line of credit at </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">1.2</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">%.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Realized and unrealized gains and losses on contracts intended to hedge specific forecasted transactions or commitments, if any, that are designated and qualify for hedge accounting are deferred and recorded as a component of accumulated other comprehensive loss and accounted for as part of the transaction. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Contracts are recorded at fair value on the balance sheet as a component of other current assets or accrued expenses and other liabilities.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;">Stock-Based Compensation:</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Company recognizes stock-based employment compensation arrangements based on the estimated fair value of stock-based awards exchanged for employee services received and recognizes compensation cost based on the fair value of the award on the date of grant, recognized ratably over the requisite service period for awards expected to vest. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The service period is the period over which the employee performs the related services, which is normally the same as the vesting period.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;">Income Taxes:</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Provisions for Federal, state and non-U.S. income taxes are calculated on reported income before income taxes based on current tax law and also include, in the current period, the cumulative effect of any changes in tax rates from those used previously in determining deferred tax assets and liabilities. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Such provisions differ from the amounts currently receivable or payable because certain items of income and expense are recognized in different time periods for financial reporting purposes than for income tax purposes. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Significant judgment is required in determining income tax provisions and evaluating tax positions.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Company records a liability associated with an uncertain income tax benefit, for a position taken or intended to be taken, if we determine that it is not more likely than not that such benefit will be sustained upon review of the taxing authority. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Company also records a tax position as the largest amount of benefit that is greater than </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">fifty</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> percent likely of being realized upon ultimate settlement.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;">Basic and Diluted Net Income Per Share:</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Basic net income per share is computed by dividing net income by the weighted average number of total shares of Class A and Class B common stock outstanding during the year. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Diluted net income per share is computed by dividing net income by diluted weighted average shares outstanding. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Diluted weighted average shares reflect the dilutive effect, if any, of potential common shares. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">To the extent that their effect is dilutive, potential common shares include common stock options and non-vested equity shares based on the treasury stock method. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">There is no anti-dilutive effect of securities for the three years ended </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">December 29, 2012</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;">Environmental Contingencies:</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Company is subject to contingencies pursuant to environmental laws and regulations under various state, Federal and foreign laws, including CERCLA. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Company typically estimates potential costs based on information obtained from the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, or counterpart state agency and/or</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> studies prepared by independent consultants, including the total estimated costs for the site and the expected cost-sharing, if any, with other &#x201C;potentially responsible parties,&#x201D; and the Company accrues liabilities when they are probable and estimable.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;">New Accounting Pronouncements</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;">:</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">In September 2011, the Financial Accounting Standards Board (&#x201C;FASB&#x201D;) issued an Accounting Standards Update (&#x201C;ASU&#x201D;) which simplifies how companies test goodwill for impairment.&nbsp;&nbsp;The ASU permits an entity to first assess qualitative factors to determine whether it is more likely than not that the fair value of a reporting unit is less than its carrying amount as a basis for determining whether it is necessary to perform the two-step goodwill impairment test described in the goodwill accounting standard.&nbsp;&nbsp;The amendments are effective for annual and interim goodwill impairment tests performed for fiscal years beginning after December 15, 2011. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> The Company adopted this pronouncement in 2012.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">In July 2012, the FASB issued an ASU which expanded the scope of this valuation testing methodology to include all indefinite-lived assets and is effective for annual and interim impairment tests performed for fiscal years beginning after September 15, 2012.&nbsp;&nbsp;We do not expect the new ASU to have a material effect on our financial position, results of operations or cash flows.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:18pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">NOTE C - RESTRUCTURING CHARGES</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">In 2008, the Company restructured Cross Accessory Division ("CAD") Lincoln based manufacturing operations in order to increase its competitiveness in the global marketplace by further leveraging the investment in China manufacturing operations. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Company also closed several underperforming retail stores and reduced headcount at its Lincoln facility. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">These restructuring programs moved Lincoln manufacturing operations to the Company's China facility and reduced the total retail store count by </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">four</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">. &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Approximately </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">50</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> manufacturing positions and </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">27</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> sales and administrative positions in the United States, and </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">four</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> sales and administrative positions in the United Kingdom were affected by these programs. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">In 2009, the Company expanded its restructuring efforts to further reduce headcount at its Lincoln and European facilities. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Company incurred pre-tax restructuring charges of approximately $</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">4.4</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> million since the inception of these programs. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Of this $4.4 million, approximately $</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">2.4</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> million was for severance and related expenses and approximately $</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">2.0</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> million was for transition and other costs.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp; &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Restructuring charges paid in fiscal 2010 were</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> $0.8 million.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;No restructuring charges were incurred in fiscal 2010, 2011 or 2012.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">NOTE D - GOODWILL AND OTHER INTANGIBLE ASSETS</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Goodwill and indefinite-lived intangible assets are not amortized but are subject to annual impairment tests, more frequently if events or circumstances occur that would indicate a potential decline in their fair value. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Company has identified two reporting units, consisting of the CAD and COG segments. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Company performs the assessment annually during the fourth quarter or on an interim basis if potential impairment indicators arise. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The fair value of the reporting unit's goodwill is determined using </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">accepted accounting standard methodologies </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">and the fair value of other indefinite-lived intangible assets, consisting of two COG segment trade names, is determined using a forward relief from royalty method.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">In 201</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">2</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, 201</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">1</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> and 20</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">10</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, the Company's annual impairment tests indicated that all remaining goodwill and indefinite-</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">lived intangibles were not impaired.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp; &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The cumulative goodwill impairment loss of $</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">3.9</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> million related to the CAD segment.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">At </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">December 29, 2012</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">December 31, 2011</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, the carrying value of goodwill was approximately $</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">15.3</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> million</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;The entire </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">goodwill </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">balance </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">is </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">related to the COG segment</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">11.9</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> million</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> of it, the goodwill resulting from the 2008 acquisition of Native, is</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> expected to be tax deductible.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp; &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">As the goodwill is all U.S. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">D</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">ollar denominated, there</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> is no translation adjustment. </font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">NOTE E - LINE OF CREDIT</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Company maintains a $</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">40</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">.0</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> million revolving line of credit with Bank of America, N.A. (the &#x201C;Bank&#x201D;).&nbsp;&nbsp;Under the line of credit agreement, the Bank </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">agreed to make loans to the Company in an aggregate amount not to exceed $40</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">.0</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> million, including up to $</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">10</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">.0</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> million equivalent in Eurocurrency loans denominated in pounds sterling or Euro (&#x201C;Eurocurrency Loans&#x201D;) and up to $</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">30</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">.0</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> million of other committed loans to the Company (&#x201C;Committed Loans&#x201D;) at any time. As part of the aggregate availability, the Bank may also issue up to $</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">7.5</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> million in letters of credit. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Subject to the limits on availability and the other terms and conditions of this credit agreement, amounts may be borrowed, repaid and reborrowed without penalty. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">This credit facility matures </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">on</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">July 28, 2013</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">T</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">he interest rate for the Committed Loans will be, at the Company's option, either (i) the London Interbank Offered Rate (&#x201C;LIBOR&#x201D;) plus an applicable margin or (ii) the higher of the federal funds rate plus </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">50</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> basis points or the Bank's prime rate plus an applicable margin. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The interest rate for any Eurocurrency Loans will be an interest settlement rate for deposits in pounds sterling or Euro plus an applicable margin. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The applicable margin for LIBOR and Eurocurrency loans will be an amount between </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">1.75</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">% and </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">2.25</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">%, and the applicable margin for federal funds or the Bank's prime rate will be an amount between </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">0.25</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">% and </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">0.75</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">%, which will vary from time to time based upon the Company's consolidated leverage ratio.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Under the line of credit agreement, the Company has agreed to comply with certain affirmative and negative covenants. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The most restrictive covenant requires the Company to maintain a maximum ratio of consolidated funded indebtedness to consolidated adjusted EBITDA over any four-quarter period. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The agreement requires the Company to maintain a minimum consolidated tangible net worth, computed at each year end, a maximum level of capital expenditures, each of which is calculated in accordance with the agreement. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Amounts due under the credit agreement are guaranteed by certain domestic and foreign subsidiaries of the Company. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Amounts due are also secured by a pledge of the assets of the Company and those of certain of its domestic subsidiaries.</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">In the third quarter of 2010, the Company entered into a forward interest rate swap agreement with an initial notional amount of $15.0 million and a term of three years.&nbsp;&nbsp;This swap effectively fixes the interest rate on a portion of the Company&#x2019;s line of credit at approximately </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">1.2</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">%.&nbsp;&nbsp;The item being hedged is the first interest payment to be made on $15.0 million of principal expected to occur each month beginning March 31, 2011.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company measures hedge ineffectiveness using the &#x201C;hypothetical&#x201D; derivative method.&nbsp;&nbsp;This swap has been designated a cash flow hedge and the effect of the mark-to-market valuation is recorded as an adjustment, net of tax, to accumulated other comprehensive loss.&nbsp;&nbsp;From inception to December 29, 2012, the effect of the mark-to-market valuations, net of tax, was an unrealized loss of approximatel</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">y $0.1 m</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">illion and is included as a component of accumulated other comprehensive loss.</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Company decreased the discount rate on domestic</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> and foreign</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> pla</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">ns in 2012 to reflect market interest rate conditions.&nbsp;&nbsp;In establishing the long-term rate of return on assets assumption of 7.8%, th</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">e Company indexed its targeted allocation percentage by asset category against the long-term expected returns on the frozen domestic plan for those asset categories. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">That weighted-average return approximate</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">s 7.8%.&nbsp;&nbsp;The C</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">ompany monitors investment results against benchmarks such as the Russell 1000 Growth Index and the Russell 2000 Value Index for the equity portion of the portfolio and the Barclays Capital US Long Credit A+ Index for fixed income investments. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Meeting or exceeding those benchmarks over time would provide a reasonable expectation of achieving </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">the 7.8%</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> assumption.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The investment objective of the Plan is to exceed the actuarial long-term rate of return on assets assumpt</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">ion of 7.8</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">%. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">To that end, it is the Plan's practice to invest the assets in accordance with the targeted allocation established for each asset category. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">These targeted asset allocation ranges have been established in accordance with the overall risk and return objectives of the portfolio. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Plan employs other risk management practices that stress diversification and liquidity. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">For equity investments, no more than 10% of the equity portfolio can be invested in one issuer and typically no more than 20% of equity assets can be invested in one industry. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Shares must be listed on major stock exchanges to assure liquidity. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Debt securities are similarly governed by risk management rules. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">No more than 5% of the total portfolio may be invested in one issuer (except the United States government), and no one issuer can exceed 5% of the outstanding shares of that issuer. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">There are also quality ratings associated with debt securities that the Plan managers must adhere to. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Certain assets or transactions are prohibited in the management of Plan assets, such as commodities, real estate (except mutual funds or REITS), venture capital, private placements, purchasing securities on margin and short selling.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Company made cash contributions in 201</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">2</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> of approximately </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$5.8</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;m</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">illion to its defined benefit pension plans, </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$2.5 million of which was an additional voluntary contribution</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company expects to co</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">ntribute $2.1 million to its defined benefit pension plans in 2013.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The fair value framework requires the categorization of pension plan assets into three levels based upon the assumptions (inputs) used to price the pension plan assets. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Level 1 provides the most reliable measure of fair value, whereas Level 3 generally requires significant management judgment. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The three levels are defined as follows:</font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">NOTE I - OMNIBUS INCENTIVE PLAN (THE &#x201C;OI PLAN&#x201D;)</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Company's OI Plan permits the Compensation Committee of the Board of Directors of the Company to grant various long-term incentive awards, generally equity based, to officers and key employees from one pool of reserved shares. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The OI Plan provides for grants of awards, including but not limited to Non-Qualified Stock Options, at an exercise price determined by the Compensation Committee; Stock Appreciation Rights, which are rights to receive an amount equal to the increase, between the date of grant and the date of exercise, in the fair market value of the number of shares of common stock subject to the Stock Appreciation Right; Non-Vested Equity Shares, which are common shares that have certain conditions attached to them that must be satisfied in order to have unencumbered rights to them; and Performance Awards, which are awards in common shares or cash. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The OI Plan has no definite expiration date but may be terminated by the Board of Directors at any time. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">At </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">December 29, 2012</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, there w</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">ere </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">1,646,586</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> shares reserved and </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">537,596</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> shares avail</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">able to be issued under the OI Plan.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The fair value of each stock option granted under the Company's OI Plan was estimated on the date of grant using the Black-Scholes option-pricing model. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">It should be noted that the option-pricing model used was designed to value readily tradable stock options with relatively short lives. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The options granted to employees are not tradable and have contractual lives of up to </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">ten</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> years unless employment is terminated. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">However, management believes that the assumptions used and the model applied to value the awards yield a reasonable estimate of the fair value of the grants made under the circumstances. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">No stock options were granted in 2012.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">At </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">December 29, 2012</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, the total un</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">amortized expense</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> for </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">stock options </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">under the OI Plan was </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">appro</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">ximately $</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">0.1</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> million.&nbsp;&nbsp;O</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">ther</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> information related to stock options follows:</font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">At </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">December 29, 2012</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">December 31, 2011</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, undistributed earnings of foreign subsidiaries amounted to approximatel</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">y $</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">39.9</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> millio</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">n and $</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">35.5</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> million, respectively. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">These earnings could become subject to additional tax if they are remitted as dividends or if certain other circumstances exist. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The amount of additional taxes that might be payable on the undistributed foreign earnings </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">of $39.9 million approximates $9.5 milli</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">on. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">This amount has not been recorded because it is the Company's intention to permanently invest the remainder of the undistributed earnings of its foreign subsidiaries in the growth of business outside the United States.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">At December 29, 2012, the Company had state net operating loss carryforwards of approximately $23.6 million, which expire in fiscal years from 2013 to 2031.&nbsp;&nbsp;Net operating loss carryforwards for certain foreign subsidiaries were approximately $3.8 million for tax purposes.&nbsp;&nbsp;A portion of these losses will expire in fiscal years from 2013 to 2025 and a portion does not expire.&nbsp;&nbsp;A valuation allowance has been provided for the foreign and state net operating losses and temporary differences that are estimated to expire before they are utilized.&nbsp;&nbsp;The decrease of $</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">0.8</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> million in 2012 and the increase of $0.3 million in 2011 in the valuation allowance primarily related to changes in state deferred tax assets.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Deferred income taxes arise from temporary differences between the tax and financial statement recognition of revenue</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> and expense. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">In evaluating our ability to recover our deferred tax assets within the jurisdiction from which they arise we consider all available positive and negative evidence, including reversals of deferred tax liabilities, projected future taxable income, tax planning strategies and recent financial operations. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">It is management's assertion based on the evaluation of this evidence that it is more likely than not that sufficient future taxable income will be generated to realize the tax benefit of the deferred tax assets, net of the valuation allowance.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

		</p>

					<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0.05pt;text-align:center; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
						<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$</font></p>
				</td>
				<td valign="middle" style="width:07.80%;border-top:1pt solid #000000 ;border-left:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-right:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;background-color: #auto;;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-align:right;" nowrap="nowrap"><div style="float:left"></div>27,279&nbsp;

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Company was named as one of approximately ninety defendants in a contribution suit brought by CCL/Unilever relating to the J.M. Mills Landfill Site (the &#x201C;Site&#x201D;), which is part of the Peterson/Puritan Superfund Site in Cumberland, Rhode Island. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">These complaints alleged that the Company was liable under the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation and Liability Act ("CERCLA") for contribution for Site investigation costs. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Company has reached settlement of the case and paid a settlement amount of approximately $0.2 million in 2010.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Company expects that the Federal Environmental Protection Agency ("EPA") will select a remedy for the Site in 201</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">3</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">. &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">At that time, the EPA will initiate an administrative process (the "Special Notice Process") pursuant to CERCLA whereby the EPA will request that those entities that the EPA contends arranged for the disposal of hazardous materials at the Site (the PRPs), undertake the selected remedy at the Site. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The EPA contends that the Company is a PRP at the Site. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">During the Special Notice Process, the Company and the other PRPs will engage in negotiations with the EPA regarding the remedy, and among themselves regarding the contribution of each PRP to overall remediation costs. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Neither the cost of the remedy nor the identity of all PRPs is known at this time. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Therefore it is not possible to assess the outcome of the Special Notice Process as it may relate to the Company's contribution to remediation costs.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Company is involved in various other litigation and legal matters that have arisen in the ordinary course of business. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">To its knowledge, management believes that the ultimate resolution of any of those existing matters will not have a material</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> adverse effect on the Company's consolidated financial position or results of operations.</font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Holders of Class A common stock have the right to elect one-third of the number of directors from time to time fixed by the holders of Class A and Class B common stock voting together as a single class. Holders of Class B common stock have the right to elect the remaining directors. Class A and Class B common stock vote together as a single class to reserve shares to be issued pursuant to options granted with respect to the acquisition of assets or shares of another company under certain circumstances. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Except as described above or as otherwise required by law, all voting power is vested in the holders of Class B common stock.</font>

		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">REPORT OF INDEPENDENT REGISTERED PUBLIC ACCOUNTING FIRM</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">To the Board of Directors and Shareholders of</font><br /><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">A.T. Cross Company</font><br /><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Lincoln, Rhode Island</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">We have audited the internal control over financial reporting of A.T. Cross Company and subsidiaries (the &#x201C;Company&#x201D;) as of </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">December 29, 2012</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, based on criteria established in </font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Internal Control - Integrated Framework </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company's management is responsible for maintaining effective internal control over financial reporting and for </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">their</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> assessment of the effectiveness of internal control over financial reporting, included in the accompanying Management's Report on Internal Control over Financial Reporting.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our responsibility is to express an opinion on the Company's internal control over financial reporting based on our audit.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">We conducted our audit in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States).&nbsp;&nbsp;Those standards require that we plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether effective internal control over financial reporting was maintained in all material respects.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our audit included obtaining an understanding of internal control over financial reporting, assessing the risk that a material weakness exists, testing and evaluating the design and operating effectiveness of internal control based on the assessed risk, and performing such other procedures as we considered necessary in the circumstances.&nbsp;&nbsp;We believe that our audit provides a reasonable basis for our opinion.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">A company's internal control over financial reporting is a process designed by, or under the supervision of, the company's principal executive and principal financial officers, or persons performing similar functions, and effected by the company's board of directors, management, and other personnel to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements for external purposes in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles.&nbsp;&nbsp;A company's internal control over financial reporting includes those policies and procedures that (1) pertain to the maintenance of records that, in reasonable detail, accurately and fairly reflect the transactions and dispositions of the assets of the company; (2) provide reasonable assurance that transactions are recorded as necessary to permit preparation of financial statements in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles, and that receipts and expenditures of the company are being made only in accordance with authorizations of management and directors of the company; and (3) provide reasonable assurance regarding prevention or timely detection of unauthorized acquisition, use, or disposition of the company's assets that could have a material effect on the financial statements.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Because of the inherent limitations of internal control over financial reporting, including the possibility of collusion or improper management override of controls, material misstatements due to error or fraud may not be prevented or detected on a timely basis.&nbsp;&nbsp;Also, projections of any evaluation of the effectiveness of the internal control over financial reporting to future periods are subject to the risk that the controls may become inadequate because of changes in conditions, or that the degree of compliance with the policies or procedures may deteriorate. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">In our opinion, the Company maintained, in all material respects, effective internal control over financial reporting as of </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">December 29, 2012</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, based on the criteria established in </font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Internal Control - Integrated Framework </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">We have also audited, in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States) the </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">consolidated financial statements of the Company as of and for the year ended </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">December 29, 2012</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> and our report dated March </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">13</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, 20</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">1</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">3</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> expressed an unqualified opinion on those financial statements</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">. &nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ; font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
